problem_type: Set Partitioning: select some of the n candidate options so that each of the m tasks is covered by exactly one selected option, minimizing the total cost of the selected options (minimize Σ costs[j]·x[j]).

decisions.business: Whether a selection of options satisfying "every task is covered exactly once" was found. true means a feasible solution is given; false reports that the instance has no feasible solution.
decisions.completeness: Required. When the instance has no feasible partition (e.g., some task is not in any covers[j], or n=0 and m>0), set false; otherwise set true and give the complete selection in x.

decisions.business: Whether each candidate option is selected: x[j]=1 means option j is selected; x[j]=0 means it is not.
decisions.shape: When feasible=true, list[int] of length n, indexed by option index 0..n-1, each element 0 or 1; when feasible=false, null.
decisions.example: For n=3, m=3, costs=[2.5, 1.0, 3.0], covers=[[0,1],[2],[1,2]]: x=[1, 1, 0] (select options 0 and 1; tasks 0 and 1 are covered by option 0, task 2 by option 1)
decisions.completeness: When feasible=true, the length must be exactly n and each element must be 0 or 1. For each task r∈{0..m-1}, there must be exactly one option j with x[j]=1 and r∈covers[j]. When n=0 it is []; when m=0, all zeros is optimal. When feasible=false it must be null, with no option selection given.

decisions.business: Total cost of the selected options Σ_j costs[j]·x[j] (unit: currency units), i.e., the objective value being minimized.
decisions.shape: When feasible=true, a float scalar; when feasible=false, null.
decisions.completeness: Required when feasible=true, and must differ from Σ costs[j]·x[j] recomputed from x by at most 1e-6 (absolute tolerance). null when feasible=false.
